fittrack-mobile.title: FitTrack Mobile
fittrack-mobile.description: Cross-platform React Native fitness app featuring optimistic UI, offline-first data sync, and AI-personalized workout plans—reducing user drop-off by 40% through friction-free mid-workout logging.
features: Optimistic UI architecture with local-first caching via AsyncStorage — all workout logs persist instantly with zero visible latency
Background sync engine that reconciles offline mutations with the server, handling conflict resolution gracefully
Shared Zustand store with selector memoization, preventing unnecessary re-renders across heavy workout screens
Custom Reanimated 2 gesture handlers for swipe-to-complete sets, matching native app interaction feel

upcomingIdeas.title: AI workout coach
upcomingIdeas.description: LLM-powered rep-counting and real-time form correction using device camera and MediaPipe pose estimation—no additional hardware required.

upcomingIdeas.title: Wearable sync
upcomingIdeas.description: Apple HealthKit and Google Fit integration to auto-import heart rate, sleep, and step data—eliminating all manual logging for passive metrics.

upcomingIdeas.title: Social accountability layer
upcomingIdeas.description: Streak leaderboards, shared workout challenges, and friend-activity feeds to drive retention through social accountability loops.

upcomingIdeas.title: Adaptive periodization engine
upcomingIdeas.description: ML model that adjusts progressive overload week-over-week based on fatigue signals, missed sessions, and personal performance trends.

content.text: The fitness app market is saturated. To differentiate, FitTrack needed a mid-workout experience with near-zero friction—no loading spinners, no manual data entry with sweaty hands, and no UX dead ends between sets. The primary drop-off point was the logging screen itself.

Built on Zustand with an optimistic update pattern—every user action writes to AsyncStorage immediately and syncs to the backend silently. Reanimated 2 powers gesture-driven interactions that feel indistinguishable from native iOS/Android components, keeping perceived performance high even on mid-range devices.

portfolio-redesign.title: Conversational Developer Portfolio
portfolio-redesign.description: Command-driven personal portfolio built with Next.js App Router and Framer Motion—replacing infinite scroll with a contextual AI chat interface that surfaces projects, skills, and experience on demand.
features: Command-palette-style interface with slash-command routing — visitors type intent, not keywords
Framer Motion layout animations for seamless content transitions between project detail views
Server-rendered shell with client-side hydration — fast initial load with no layout shift (zero CLS)
JSON-driven content architecture — all portfolio data decoupled from UI components for easy updates

upcomingIdeas.title: Live Claude API integration
upcomingIdeas.description: Replace simulated responses with real Claude API calls—making the portfolio genuinely answer recruiter and client questions about specific projects, stack choices, and availability.

upcomingIdeas.title: RAG over resume & projects
upcomingIdeas.description: Embed resume, project write-ups, and GitHub READMEs into a pgvector store so the chat can retrieve and cite specific achievements in context.

upcomingIdeas.title: Visitor analytics dashboard
upcomingIdeas.description: Track which projects and questions visitors ask most — feeding insights back into which work to feature or expand in the portfolio.

upcomingIdeas.title: Voice input via Web Speech API
upcomingIdeas.description: Let mobile visitors speak queries naturally — further differentiating the experience from every static portfolio in the market.

content.text: Rethinking the portfolio as a product

Traditional portfolios force visitors to navigate a predetermined structure. This portfolio inverts that model — the visitor drives the conversation. Using Next.js App Router for SSR performance and Framer Motion for layout-aware transitions, the interface feels like a premium AI product rather than a developer resume.

hooked-on-movies.title: HookedOnMovies
hooked-on-movies.description: Full-stack media discovery platform built on Next.js with SSR/ISR, a TypeScript normalization layer across TMDB's Movie & TV APIs, and sub-second TTFB via parallel server-side data fetching.
features: TypeScript data normalization layer that reconciles inconsistent TMDB Movie vs TV Show field schemas into a single unified interface—eliminating runtime type errors across the entire app
Parallel server-side data fetching with Promise.all across multiple TMDB endpoints, cutting TTFB significantly versus sequential waterfall requests
ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) on detail pages — content stays fresh without per-request SSR cost, ideal for high-traffic title pages
Full SEO implementation: dynamic Open Graph tags, structured metadata per page, and canonical URLs for discoverability on search engines

upcomingIdeas.title: Personalized recommendation engine
upcomingIdeas.description: Replace TMDB's basic 'similar' endpoint with an embedding-based recommender (OpenAI embeddings + cosine similarity) that learns from a user's watch history and ratings.

upcomingIdeas.title: User accounts + persistent watchlists
upcomingIdeas.description: Add NextAuth.js with Google OAuth, PostgreSQL-backed watchlists, and per-user recommendation personalization that persists across sessions.

upcomingIdeas.title: Streaming availability via JustWatch API
upcomingIdeas.description: Show which platform (Netflix, Prime, Hotstar, etc.) each title is currently available on — bridging discovery to instant action.

upcomingIdeas.title: Redis edge caching for TMDB responses
upcomingIdeas.description: Cache API responses at the CDN edge with configurable Redis TTLs to eliminate redundant TMDB calls and achieve sub-100ms global response times.

content.text: HookedOnMovies is a production-quality media discovery platform with a focus on performance, type safety, and cinematic UX. Users can explore trending content, view rich metadata, watch trailers, and surface recommendations—with a UI that competes visually with commercial streaming platforms.

TMDB's API returns fundamentally different shapes for movies versus TV shows. A custom TypeScript normalization layer maps both into a single shared interface consumed across all components—eliminating defensive nullchecks throughout the codebase. Combined with Promise.all parallel fetching on the server, page data is assembled in a single round-trip rather than a waterfall.

Demonstrates end-to-end ownership of a full-stack Next.js product: API integration architecture, TypeScript system design, ISR caching strategy, SEO implementation, and a polished Framer Motion UI—all shipped as a cohesive, performant application.
